plain_english: Never say you have lost something. Say you have returned it. Your child died? They were returned. Your property was taken? It was returned. "But the person who took it is wicked." What does it matter to you who the giver assigns to take it back?
original_excerpt: Never say of anything, "I have lost it"; but, "I have returned it." Is your child dead? It is returned. Is your wife dead? She is returned.

plain_english: If you want to make progress, give up trying to control everything outside yourself. Accept being thought foolish and simple when it comes to external things. Do not wish to be admired. If others think you are somebody, distrust yourself.
original_excerpt: If you wish to make progress, be content to be thought foolish and stupid with regard to external things. Do not wish to be thought to know anything.

plain_english: Remember that you are an actor in a play. The author has given you your part — short or long, rich or poor. Your job is to play it well. Choosing the role is someone else's business.
original_excerpt: Remember that thou art an actor in a drama, of such a kind as the author pleases to make it.
